S&P 500 Sector-Rotation Portfolio Strategy

Generated 2026-07-04 10:56 UTC · Data: Yahoo Finance daily adjusted close · Backtest window: 2000-01-03 → 2026-07-02

Strategy definition

Monthly-rebalanced rotation across the S&P 500 sector SPDR ETFs: XLK, XLF, XLV, XLY, XLP, XLE, XLI, XLB, XLU (+ XLRE, XLC once eligible), ranked by a composite momentum score (equal blend of trailing 3/6/12-month returns). The top 4 sectors are held equally weighted, gated by two overlays:

  • Trend filter — Faber's 10-month SMA rule on SPY (with a 2% hysteresis band to reduce whipsaws): fully invested only while SPY's month-end close is above its trailing 10-month average; otherwise the book rotates to a synthetic cash / 13-week T-bill proxy (built from ^IRX).
  • Volatility targeting — exposure is scaled to keep the selected sector basket's trailing 20-day realised volatility near an 18% annualised target, capped at 1.15x (modest, realistic leverage financed at the cash rate) so the book de-risks automatically ahead of / during volatility spikes.

All decisions at execution date t use data available only through t−1 (no lookahead); rebalancing executes at date t's close. A 5 bps one-way cost is applied to traded turnover at every rebalance.

The full combined overlay (trend filter + vol targeting) modestly outperforms SPY on CAGR while more than halving the maximum drawdown and roughly doubling the Sharpe ratio and Calmar ratio (return per unit of drawdown risk) — precisely because it avoids the bulk of the 2000-02, 2008 and 2022 drawdowns, at the cost of lagging during some of the strongest melt-up years (2013, 2017, 2019-21, 2023-24).

2 · Scenario Ablation — Contribution of Each Overlay

Each overlay is added incrementally to isolate its marginal contribution: pure relative-momentum rotation, then + the trend/regime filter, then + volatility targeting (the final configuration used throughout this report).

5 · Monte Carlo Simulation

Reusing src.strategy.monte_carlo.run_monte_carlo and mc_summary_table unmodified (5,000 bootstrap resamples). The resampling unit here is the strategy's calendar-month portfolio return rather than a single position's P&L: this portfolio holds several sector positions concurrently, so individual trade P&Ls are not independent/sequential in the way the original BTCUSDT single-position engine assumes — monthly portfolio returns are the correct sequential, non-overlapping unit for this strategy shape.

6 · Small-Account Feasibility (€1,000 / €2,000 / €3,000)

Institutional-size backtests hide two frictions that dominate at retail scale: most EU brokers don't offer fractional ETF shares, and many charge a flat fee per order rather than a pure bps spread. Idealized assumes fractional shares and only the 5 bps turnover cost already used above; Realistic floors every position to whole shares (the rounding residual falls back to cash) and adds a flat €1.50 commission per traded ETF leg — a representative low-cost EU broker rate. Both are converted from USD to EUR day-by-day using the EUR/USD rate, so the result also reflects unhedged currency risk for a euro-based investor (Yahoo's EUR/USD history starts 2003-11; the 2000-2003 segment is held at that first observed rate as an approximation). A single-purchase SPY buy & hold at the same capital is shown as the "do nothing fancy" alternative.

At €1,000 the ~3 monthly-average traded legs mean whole-share rounding and flat commissions consume a large fraction of the strategy's edge over SPY — the drag shrinks fast as capital rises. Below roughly €3,000-5,000, a plain SPY buy & hold is very likely the more capital-efficient choice; the rotation strategy only starts to earn its complexity once per-leg costs are a small fraction of position size.

Backtest only — not investment advice. Yahoo Finance adjusted-close data; ETF expense ratios and bid/ask spread beyond the modelled 5 bps turnover cost are not included. Past performance, in-sample or out-of-sample, does not guarantee future results; the trend filter and volatility overlay are rule-based and can underperform SPY in sustained, low-volatility bull markets (as shown in Section 1). Sector universe: XLK, XLF, XLV, XLY, XLP, XLE, XLI, XLB, XLU (+ XLRE, XLC once eligible). Cash proxy: synthetic daily-accrual NAV built from the ^IRX 13-week T-bill discount yield.
